newsitem.title: PERU: Lima raid sends Fujimori's popularity soaring.
newsitem.headline: Lima raid sends Fujimori's popularity soaring.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori's popularity has nearly doubled after a successful raid on the besieged Japanese ambassador's house in Lima, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.

The survey by polling agency Apoyo SA conducted the day after the raid showed Fujimori's popularity had shot up overnight to 67 percent from 38 percent four days ago, Apoyo director Alfredo Torres said.
Those who disapproved of his performance as president fell to 22 percent from 47 percent four days ago, said Apoyo.

The poll of 420 people in metropolitan Lima, where about one-third of Peruvians live, showed 84 percent approved of the assault on the residence, in which elite commandos rescued all but one of the 72 hostages alive. Only 10 percent disapproved.
Two soldiers and all 14 of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrillas died in the 40-minute gunbattle.
"There is clearly support -- whether it lasts or not -- for how the president has dealt with the conflict," said Torres on Panamericana television.

Fujimori's approval rating had held steady at about 50 percent for the duration of the siege, which began on Dec. 17, but suddenly plunged to 38 percent last week as negotiations to free the hostages languished.

The new poll also showed strong support for the role that Fujimori's controversial National Intelligence Service was perceived to have played in ending the siege. Its shadowy chief Vladimiro Montesinos made a rare public appearance on Wednesday when he visited the liberated residence.
Eigthy-six percent of respondents said they supported the SIN's role in the crisis, with six percent disapproving, and 89 percent saying they supported the military's role in the crisis.
Torres did not say what the poll's margin of error was.
